title: FieldOps Pro AI Audit Record
description: One JSON Lines record per Anthropic API invocation. Written by SCRIPTS/AI/FieldOps-AIClient.psm1 to LOGS/ai-audit.jsonl. See DOCS/AI-INTEGRATION.md for the hash verification procedure.

schemaVersion.description: 1.1 adds the optional system_sha256 field to 1.0. Records without it remain valid, so the change is backward compatible.

ts.description: ISO 8601 with offset, of when the call completed.

model.description: Model identifier actually used for the call.

model_override.description: True when the caller supplied an explicit model rather than accepting the tier default.

est_cost_usd.description: Cost estimated before the call, used for ceiling enforcement.

cost_usd.description: Actual cost from the usage the API reported. Zero when the call was refused or failed before billing.

cost_variance.description: cost_usd minus est_cost_usd. POSITIVE means the estimate came in LOW, which is the direction that matters: the ceiling was consulted against a figure smaller than reality. Design doc risk 6.5-Risk-1 calls for tuning on this series.

prompt_sha256.description: SHA-256 over the UTF-8 bytes, WITHOUT byte order mark, of the user prompt exactly as sent. Lowercase hex. A hash whose input is not precisely specified cannot be reproduced by an auditor and is therefore decorative; see DOCS/AI-INTEGRATION.md for the verification procedure.

system_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the system prompt, same encoding rule as prompt_sha256. Null when no system prompt was sent. ADDED IN 1.1. This supports provenance rather than tamper detection: it lets an operator demonstrate that a set of machines was assessed under identical instructions, which is the question a compliance auditor actually asks. It is not a security control, since anyone able to alter the system prompt can equally alter the writer that records it.

response_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the response text, same encoding rule. Null when no response was received.

tech.description: Pseudonymous technician identifier: a truncated SHA-256 of the technician name. Pseudonymous, NOT anonymous -- a short name space is brute-forceable by anyone holding a candidate list. It prevents casual disclosure in a shared log; it does not defeat a determined re-identification attempt, and should not be described to customers as if it does.

failure_reason.description: Machine-readable reason from the client's failure contract, e.g. EstimateExceedsCeiling.
